# Specialists and shared knowledge · M07

Compare ways to build resilience through coaching, starting knowledge and work assignment. Up to six coaching periods can be moved on the timeline with mouse, touch or arrow keys, then edited through labelled controls. One-backup, two-backup and relay examples request equal total coaching time. Up to eight inclusive absence windows allow temporary, permanent or overlapping absences. Initial and later demand are editable for every skill; both plans use identical seeded variation.

Each present person has one week of time. Concurrent coaching is scaled by the more constrained participant so work, coaching and idle time sum to that week. Absent participants or self-coaching block a session without consuming time. All sessions use starting-of-week knowledge: newly learned knowledge cannot be relayed immediately. Coaching gain is 0.65 × actual time × positive skill gap; work also teaches slowly. Gains arrive at week end and persist. The inspector exposes time allocation, blocked/scaled periods and queues. Coverage includes all three skills with an explicit 60% threshold.

Pinned plans freeze skills, assignments and coaching; demand and absences remain shared. Changed starting knowledge is flagged. Legacy saves retain their results and migrate the original coaching period and permanent absence. Local save, Undo, recovery/cross-tab pause and Markdown/JSON import/export preserve comparisons, conditions and decision notes. Imports validate before replacement; Undo restores the previous experiment.

Fictional divisible, independent work; no forgetting, coordination, hiring, motivation or certification. Tests cover accounting, delayed learning, overlapping commitments and absences, migration, matched comparisons and portable work. Two backups outperform one in the default absence scenario; that ranking reverses when the specialist remains. With full starting knowledge, coaching costs output without improving capability. These counterexamples prevent a single prescribed strategy.
